newsitem.title: USA: Oncogene, Hoechst to develop inducer.
newsitem.headline: Oncogene, Hoechst to develop inducer.

text.p: Pharmaceutical company Oncogene Science Inc said Wednesday it would work with Germany's Hoechst Marion Roussel, a Hoechst AG affiliate, to develop an inducer to help treat anemia.

Oncogene said it signed a collaborative research and license agreement with Hoechst to develop an orally active, small molecule inducer of erythropoietin gene expression for the treatment of anemia caused by chronic renal failure or associated with chemotherapy for AIDS and cancer, it said.

Under terms of the agreement, Oncogene said it will receive up to $30 million in research funding, milestone payments and success fees, together with royalties on the sales by Hoechst Marion Roussel of any approved products resulting from the collaboration.
